promises.quote: We will continue to be strongly supportive of this initiative and support the need for early escalation of care for those patients in whom it is not possible to undertake vital signs.
promises.summary: Support early escalation of care for patients where vital signs cannot be taken.

promises.quote: We have been collaborating with NHS England and the Royal College of Nursing to develop a single national PEWS for England since 2018 and are supportive of equivalent processes across the UK
promises.summary: Develop a single national PEWS for England

promises.quote: Emergency clinicians with responsibility for the care of children receive training in how to assess risk and immediately manage children's mental health needs and support their family/carers
promises.summary: Train emergency clinicians in paediatric mental health risk assessment

promises.quote: The trust emergency department electronic patient records do not show how many times a patient has presented to hospital with the same signs and symptoms during their current illness
promises.summary: Improve electronic patient records to track repeat presentations

concerns.quote: It was difficult for the nursing staff to obtain Daniel's observations because he was so distressed. That was understandable, but because of the long wait in a busy department, it meant that on the fourth attendance Daniel did not have a full set of observations for over four hours and shortly afterwards suffered a catastrophic cardiovascular compromise. The trust emergency department electronic patient records do not show how many times a patient has presented to hospital with the same signs and symptoms during their current illness - and of course this may be the case in other emergency departments.

reports.title: Viviana-Ray Butnaru: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: There appears to be a lack of local or national guidelines assisting those assessing patients in an accident and emergency and paediatric environment to assess the correct pathway for identifying and investigating those who may present with heart related issues such as myocarditis
concerns.hazard: lack of guidelines for identifying heart related issues in A&E paediatric environment

concerns.quote: Raising awareness of the existence of Parvovirus considering the surge of this virus in children post the Covid 19 pandemic
concerns.hazard: lack of awareness of Parvovirus surge in children

concerns.quote: Chest X rays which showed cardiomegaly were not reported officially by a radiologist until several days later
concerns.hazard: delayed official reporting of cardiomegaly on chest X ray

concerns.quote: Underlying causes for metabolic acidosis were not fully explored
concerns.hazard: incomplete exploration of metabolic acidosis causes

concerns.quote: Incomplete documentation to be addressed to include all updates from nursing staff in relation to observations and escalations; and handovers from the medical team to one another to be clearly recorded
concerns.hazard: incomplete documentation of observations and handovers

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that failing to obtain or record nursing observations in pediatric emergency care can lead to serious harm. They share the concern that absent observations should be treated as abnormal and escalated promptly.
links.earlier_quote: It was difficult for the nursing staff to obtain Daniel's observations because he was so distressed. That was understandable, but because of the long wait in a busy department, it meant that on the fourth attendance Daniel did not have a full set of observations for over four hours and shortly afterwards suffered a catastrophic cardiovascular compromise.
links.later_quote: The lack of serial nursing observations was a fundamental omission from Finlay's care.
links.promise_quote: The Trust has ratified and disseminated an updated guideline for recording and escalating physiological observations in children and young people. This includes guidance for staff that the inability to obtain observations should be considered and escalated in the same way as abnormal observations.
